topic: Easing back into Pilates after a back flare-up

slides.headline: Back settling? Ease into Pilates again
slides.sub: How to ease back into Pilates after a flare-up without starting from scratch.

slides.title: Wait for the worst to settle
slides.body: You don't need zero pain to start moving again. Most people do well once they can walk, sit and sleep reasonably. Gentle movement often helps a flare-up settle faster than rest.

slides.title: Tell your instructor first
slides.body: Let your Pilates instructor or physio know what happened, when it started and what aggravates it. They can adjust springs, positions and range so the session meets you where you are.

slides.title: Start lower and shorter
slides.body: Try a shorter session with lighter springs and smaller ranges. Leave curls, deep twists or heavy loads for later. The aim is to finish feeling the same or better, not worse.

slides.title: Use the 24-hour check
slides.body: Mild soreness that eases by the next day is usually fine. If your back is clearly worse for longer than that, drop the load a little next time rather than stopping altogether.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain spreading down a leg with numbness or weakness, pain that keeps climbing, or changes in bladder or bowel control need medical attention before you get back to the reformer.

slides.headline: Ready to get back on the reformer?
slides.body: Our Pilates team reviews how your back is going and adjusts your program so you can build up steadily again.

caption:
A back flare-up doesn't mean giving up Pilates. It usually means changing how you do it for a little while.

Once the worst has settled and you can walk, sit and sleep reasonably, gentle movement often helps. Start with shorter sessions, lighter springs and smaller ranges, and use a simple rule: if your back feels the same or better within 24 hours, you're on track.

Let your instructor know what happened so they can adapt your session. Leg numbness or weakness, pain that keeps climbing, or bladder or bowel changes need medical attention first.

At Hybrid Physiotherapy, our Pilates team works alongside our physios, so your program can change as your back does. Book online via the link in bio.
